title: अशीतितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 80 · Seventh day: Yudhishthira and Abhimanyu

summary.en: At midday Yudhishthira attacks Shrutayus, and Kripa and Abhimanyu fight fiercely. The Kauravas surround Arjuna with arrows and a great bloody battle follows.
summary.kn: ಮಧ್ಯಾಹ್ನ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ ಶ್ರುತಾಯುಸ್ಸನ ಮೇಲೆ ದಾಳಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಕೃಪ ಮತ್ತು ಅಭಿಮನ್ಯು ಉಗ್ರವಾಗಿ ಹೋರಾಡುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಕೌರವರು ಅರ್ಜುನನನ್ನು ಬಾಣಗಳಿಂದ ಸುತ್ತುವರಿಯುತ್ತಾರೆ, ರಕ್ತಮಯ ಮಹಾಯುದ್ಧ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.
summary.hi: मध्याह्न में युधिष्ठिर श्रुतायु पर आक्रमण करते हैं, और कृप तथा अभिमन्यु उग्र युद्ध करते हैं। कौरव अर्जुन को बाणों से घेर लेते हैं और रक्तरंजित महायुद्ध होता है।
summary.te: మధ్యాహ్నం యుధిష్ఠిరుడు శ్రుతాయువుపై దాడి చేస్తాడు; కృపుడు, అభిమన్యుడు భీకరంగా పోరాడతారు. కౌరవులు అర్జునుని బాణాలతో చుట్టుముడతారు, రక్తసిక్త మహాయుద్ధం జరుగుతుంది.
summary.ta: நண்பகலில் யுதிஷ்டிரர் ஸ்ருதாயுவைத் தாக்க, கிருபரும் அபிமன்யுவும் கடுமையாகப் போரிடுகின்றனர். கௌரவர் அர்ஜுனனை அம்புகளால் சூழ, இரத்தம் பெருகும் பெரும்போர் நடக்கிறது.
summary.ml: ഉച്ചയ്ക്ക് യുധിഷ്ഠിരൻ ശ്രുതായുസ്സിനെ ആക്രമിക്കുന്നു; കൃപരും അഭിമന്യുവും ഘോരമായി പൊരുതുന്നു. കൗരവർ അർജുനനെ അമ്പുകൾകൊണ്ട് വളയുന്നു; വലിയ രക്തരൂഷിത യുദ്ധം തുടരുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 6.80; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 26 2021

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा मध्यं प्राप्ते दिवाकरे ।
श्रुतायुषमभिप्रेक्ष्य चोदयामास वाजिनः ॥

meaning.en: Then, when the sun reached midday, King Yudhishthira saw Shrutayus and urged on his horses.

verses.text:
अभ्यधावत्ततो राजा श्रुतायुषमरिंदमम् ।
विनिघ्नन्सायकैस्तीक्ष्णैर्नवभिर्नतपर्वभिः ॥

meaning.en: The king rushed at Shrutayus, the enemy-tamer, striking him with nine sharp, bent-jointed arrows.

verses.text:
स संवार्य रणे राजा प्रेषितान्धर्मसूनुना ।
शरान्सप्त महेष्वासः कौन्तेयाय समर्पयत् ॥

meaning.en: Holding off the arrows sent by the son of Dharma, that great bowman king shot seven arrows at the son of Kunti.

verses.text:
ते तस्य कवचं भित्त्वा पपुः शोणितमाहवे ।
असूनिव विचिन्वन्तो देहे तस्य महात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: They pierced his armor and drank his blood in the battle, as if searching for the life in that great-souled man's body.

verses.text:
पाण्डवस्तु भृशं विद्धस्तेन राज्ञा महात्मना ।
रणे वराहकर्णेन राजानं हृदि विव्यधे ॥

meaning.en: Hard struck by that great-souled king, the Pandava in the battle pierced the king in the heart with a boar-eared arrow.

verses.text:
अथापरेण भल्लेन केतुं तस्य महात्मनः ।
रथश्रेष्ठो रथात्तूर्णं भूमौ पार्थो न्यपातयत् ॥

meaning.en: Then with another barbed arrow, Partha, the best of charioteers, quickly brought that great-souled man's banner down to the ground.

verses.text:
केतुं निपतितं दृष्ट्वा श्रुतायुः स तु पार्थिवः ।
पाण्डवं विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णै राजन्विव्याध सप्तभिः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing his banner fallen, King Shrutayus pierced the Pandava with seven sharp arrows, O king.

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधात्प्रजज्वाल धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।
यथा युगान्ते भूतानि धक्ष्यन्निव हुताशनः ॥

meaning.en: Then Yudhishthira, son of Dharma, blazed up with anger like fire at the end of an age, ready to burn all creatures.

verses.text:
क्रुद्धं तु पाण्डवं दृष्ट्वा देवगन्धर्वराक्षसाः ।
प्रविव्यथुर्महाराज व्याकुलं चाप्यभूज्जगत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the Pandava enraged, the gods, gandharvas and rakshasas trembled, O great king, and the world was troubled.

verses.text:
सर्वेषां चैव भूतानामिदमासीन्मनोगतम् ।
त्रीँल्लोकानद्य संक्रुद्धो नृपोऽयं धक्ष्यतीति वै ॥

meaning.en: All beings thought, "This king, enraged, will burn the three worlds today."

verses.text:
ऋषयश्चैव देवाश्च चक्रुः स्वस्त्ययनं महत् ।
लोकानां नृप शान्त्यर्थं क्रोधिते पाण्डवे तदा ॥

meaning.en: The sages and gods performed a great rite of blessing for the peace of the worlds, as the Pandava was angered.

verses.text:
स च क्रोधसमाविष्टः सृक्किणी परिलेलिहन् ।
दधारात्मवपुर्घोरं युगान्तादित्यसंनिभम् ॥

meaning.en: Filled with anger, licking the corners of his mouth, he bore a terrible form like the sun at the end of an age.

verses.text:
ततः सर्वाणि सैन्यानि तावकानि विशां पते ।
निराशान्यभवंस्तत्र जीवितं प्रति भारत ॥

meaning.en: Then all your armies, O lord of men, lost hope for their lives there, O Bharata.

verses.text:
स तु धैर्येण तं कोपं संनिवार्य महायशाः ।
श्रुतायुषः प्रचिच्छेद मुष्टिदेशे महद्धनुः ॥

meaning.en: But the very famous king held back that anger with steadiness, and cut Shrutayus's great bow at the grip.

verses.text:
अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं नाराचेन स्तनान्तरे ।
निर्बिभेद रणे राजा सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: Then, with the bow cut, the king pierced him with an iron arrow between the breasts as all the army watched.

verses.text:
सत्वरं चरणे राजंस्तस्य वाहान्महात्मनः ।
निजघान शरैः क्षिप्रं सूतं च सुमहाबलः ॥

meaning.en: The very mighty king quickly killed his horses with arrows at the foot of the chariot and his charioteer too.

verses.text:
हताश्वं तु रथं त्यक्त्वा दृष्ट्वा राज्ञस्तु पौरुषम् ।
विप्रदुद्राव वेगेन श्रुतायुः समरे तदा ॥

meaning.en: Abandoning his horseless chariot, having seen the king's prowess, Shrutayus then fled swiftly from the battle.

verses.text:
तस्मिञ्जिते महेष्वासे धर्मपुत्रेण संयुगे ।
दुर्योधनबलं राजन्सर्वमासीत्पराङ्मुखम् ॥

meaning.en: When that great bowman was beaten in the battle by the son of Dharma, Duryodhana's whole army turned away, O king.

verses.text:
एतत्कृत्वा महाराज धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः ।
व्यात्ताननो यथा कालस्तव सैन्यं जघान ह ॥

meaning.en: Having done this, O great king, Yudhishthira, son of Dharma, struck down your army like Death with open mouth.

verses.text:
चेकितानस्तु वार्ष्णेयो गौतमं रथिनां वरम् ।
प्रेक्षतां सर्वसैन्यानां छादयामास सायकैः ॥

meaning.en: Chekitana, the Vrishni, covered Kripa, descendant of Gotama and best of charioteers, with arrows as all the armies looked on.

verses.text:
संनिवार्य शरांस्तांस्तु कृपः शारद्वतो युधि ।
चेकितानं रणे यत्तं राजन्विव्याध पत्रिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Kripa, son of Sharadvat, warding off those arrows in the fight, pierced the vigilant Chekitana with feathered arrows, O king.

verses.text:
अथापरेण भल्लेन धनुश्चिच्छेद मारिष ।
सारथिं चास्य समरे क्षिप्रहस्तो न्यपातयत् ।
हयांश्चास्यावधीद्राजन्नुभौ च पार्ष्णिसारथी ॥

meaning.en: Then, O revered one, with another barbed arrow he cut his bow, and with quick hands felled his charioteer, and killed his horses and both his rear attendants, O king.

verses.text:
सोऽवप्लुत्य रथात्तूर्णं गदां जग्राह सात्वतः ।
स तया वीरघातिन्या गदया गदिनां वरः ।
गौतमस्य हयान्हत्वा सारथिं च न्यपातयत् ॥

meaning.en: The Satvata leapt quickly from his chariot and took up a mace; with that hero-slaying mace, best of mace-fighters, he killed Kripa's horses and felled his charioteer.

verses.text:
भूमिष्ठो गौतमस्तस्य शरांश्चिक्षेप षोडश ।
ते शराः सात्वतं भित्त्वा प्राविशन्त धरातलम् ॥

meaning.en: Standing on the ground, Kripa shot sixteen arrows at him. Those arrows pierced the Satvata and went into the ground.

verses.text:
चेकितानस्ततः क्रुद्धः पुनश्चिक्षेप तां गदाम् ।
गौतमस्य वधाकाङ्क्षी वृत्रस्येव पुरंदरः ॥

meaning.en: Enraged, Chekitana hurled the mace again, wishing to kill Kripa, as Indra hurled his at Vritra.

verses.text:
तामापतन्तीं विमलामश्मगर्भां महागदाम् ।
शरैरनेकसाहस्रैर्वारयामास गौतमः ॥

meaning.en: Kripa warded off that bright, stone-cored great mace as it came at him, with many thousands of arrows.

verses.text:
चेकितानस्ततः खड्गं कोशादुद्धृत्य भारत ।
लाघवं परमास्थाय गौतमं समुपाद्रवत् ॥

meaning.en: Then, O Bharata, Chekitana drew his sword from its sheath and, with the greatest quickness, ran at Kripa.

verses.text:
गौतमोऽपि धनुस्त्यक्त्वा प्रगृह्यासिं सुसंशितम् ।
वेगेन महता राजंश्चेकितानमुपाद्रवत् ॥

meaning.en: Kripa too cast aside his bow, took a well-sharpened sword, and ran with great speed at Chekitana, O king.

verses.text:
तावुभौ बलसंपन्नौ निस्त्रिंशवरधारिणौ ।
निस्त्रिंशाभ्यां सुतीक्ष्णाभ्यामन्योन्यं संततक्षतुः ॥

meaning.en: Those two, full of strength, holding excellent swords, cut at each other with their very sharp swords.

verses.text:
निस्त्रिंशवेगाभिहतौ ततस्तौ पुरुषर्षभौ ।
धरणीं समनुप्राप्तौ सर्वभूतनिषेविताम् ।
मूर्छयाभिपरीताङ्गौ व्यायामेन च मोहितौ ॥

meaning.en: Struck by the force of the swords, those two best of men fell to the earth that supports all beings, their limbs overcome with faintness and bewildered by the exertion.

verses.text:
ततोऽभ्यधावद्वेगेन करकर्षः सुहृत्तया ।
चेकितानं तथाभूतं दृष्ट्वा समरदुर्मदम् ।
रथमारोपयच्चैनं सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: Then Karakarsha rushed up swiftly out of friendship, and seeing Chekitana in that state, wild in battle, lifted him onto his chariot as all the army watched.

verses.text:
तथैव शकुनिः शूरः स्यालस्तव विशां पते ।
आरोपयद्रथं तूर्णं गौतमं रथिनां वरम् ॥

meaning.en: In the same way the brave Shakuni, your brother-in-law, O lord of men, quickly lifted Kripa, best of charioteers, onto his chariot.

verses.text:
सौमदत्तिं तथा क्रुद्धो धृष्टकेतुर्महाबलः ।
नवत्या सायकैः क्षिप्रं राजन्विव्याध वक्षसि ॥

meaning.en: Dhrishtaketu, the mighty, enraged, quickly struck the son of Somadatta in the chest with ninety arrows, O king.

verses.text:
सौमदत्तिरुरःस्थैस्तैर्भृशं बाणैरशोभत ।
मध्यंदिने महाराज रश्मिभिस्तपनो यथा ॥

meaning.en: With those arrows in his chest, the son of Somadatta shone greatly, like the sun at midday with its rays, O great king.

verses.text:
भूरिश्रवास्तु समरे धृष्टकेतुं महारथम् ।
हतसूतहयं चक्रे विरथं सायकोत्तमैः ॥

meaning.en: Bhurishravas in the battle took the great chariot-warrior Dhrishtaketu's charioteer and horses with excellent arrows and left him without a chariot.

verses.text:
विरथं चैनमालोक्य हताश्वं हतसारथिम् ।
महता शरवर्षेण छादयामास संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: Seeing him without a chariot, his horses and charioteer killed, he covered him in the battle with a great shower of arrows.

verses.text:
स च तं रथमुत्सृज्य धृष्टकेतुर्महामनाः ।
आरुरोह ततो यानं शतानीकस्य मारिष ॥

meaning.en: Great-minded Dhrishtaketu left that chariot and climbed onto the chariot of Shatanika, O revered one.

verses.text:
चित्रसेनो विकर्णश्च राजन्दुर्मर्षणस्तथा ।
रथिनो हेमसंनाहाः सौभद्रमभिदुद्रुवुः ॥

meaning.en: Chitrasena, Vikarna and Durmarshana, O king, those gold-armored charioteers, rushed at Subhadra's son.

verses.text:
अभिमन्योस्ततस्तैस्तु घोरं युद्धमवर्तत ।
शरीरस्य यथा राजन्वातपित्तकफैस्त्रिभिः ॥

meaning.en: Then a terrible battle took place between Abhimanyu and them, like the body's struggle against its three humors, wind, bile and phlegm, O king.

verses.text:
विरथांस्तव पुत्रांस्तु कृत्वा राजन्महाहवे ।
न जघान नरव्याघ्रः स्मरन्भीमवचस्तदा ॥

meaning.en: Having left your sons without chariots in the great battle, that tiger among men did not kill them, remembering Bhima's words.

verses.text:
ततो राज्ञां बहुशतैर्गजाश्वरथयायिभिः ।
संवृतं समरे भीष्मं देवैरपि दुरासदम् ॥

meaning.en: Then Bhishma, surrounded by many hundreds of kings with elephants, horses and chariots, hard to approach even for the gods,

verses.text:
प्रयान्तं शीघ्रमुद्वीक्ष्य परित्रातुं सुतांस्तव ।
अभिमन्युं समुद्दिश्य बालमेकं महारथम् ।
वासुदेवमुवाचेदं कौन्तेयः श्वेतवाहनः ॥

meaning.en: was seen going swiftly to protect your sons against Abhimanyu, the lone young great chariot-warrior. Seeing this, the white-horsed son of Kunti said this to Vasudeva.

verses.text:
चोदयाश्वान्हृषीकेश यत्रैते बहुला रथाः ।
एते हि बहवः शूराः कृतास्त्रा युद्धदुर्मदाः ।
यथा न हन्युर्नः सेनां तथा माधव चोदय ॥

meaning.en: Urge the horses, Hrishikesha, to where those many chariots are. Those many brave men, skilled in weapons and wild in battle, must not kill our army. Drive so that they do not, Madhava.

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः स वार्ष्णेयः कौन्तेयेनामितौजसा ।
रथं श्वेतहयैर्युक्तं प्रेषयामास संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: Spoken to thus by the son of Kunti of boundless might, the Vrishni drove the chariot with its white horses into the battle.

verses.text:
निष्टानको महानासीत्तव सैन्यस्य मारिष ।
यदर्जुनो रणे क्रुद्धः संयातस्तावकान्प्रति ॥

meaning.en: A great outcry rose in your army, O revered one, when Arjuna rode furiously in the fight toward your men.

verses.text:
समासाद्य तु कौन्तेयो राज्ञस्तान्भीष्मरक्षिणः ।
सुशर्माणमथो राजन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Reaching those kings who guarded Bhishma, the son of Kunti spoke these words to Susharman, O king.

verses.text:
जानामि त्वां युधि श्रेष्ठमत्यन्तं पूर्ववैरिणम् ।
पर्यायस्याद्य संप्राप्तं फलं पश्य सुदारुणम् ।
अद्य ते दर्शयिष्यामि पूर्वप्रेतान्पितामहान् ॥

meaning.en: I know you as the best in battle, an old enemy of ours. See today the terrible fruit of your turn that has arrived. Today I will show you your forefathers who died before.

verses.text:
एवं संजल्पतस्तस्य बीभत्सोः शत्रुघातिनः ।
श्रुत्वापि परुषं वाक्यं सुशर्मा रथयूथपः ।
न चैनमब्रवीत्किंचिच्छुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् ॥

meaning.en: Though Bibhatsu, slayer of foes, spoke so, Susharman, leader of a chariot troop, even after hearing those harsh words, said nothing to him, good or bad.

verses.text:
अभि गत्वार्जुनं वीरं राजभिर्बहुभिर्वृतः ।
पुरस्तात्पृष्ठतश्चैव पार्श्वतश्चैव सर्वतः ॥

meaning.en: Going up to the hero Arjuna, surrounded by many kings in front, behind and on both sides,

verses.text:
परिवार्यार्जुनं संख्ये तव पुत्रैः सहानघ ।
शरैः संछादयामास मेघैरिव दिवाकरम् ॥

meaning.en: and surrounding Arjuna in the battle together with your sons, O sinless one, he covered him with arrows as clouds cover the sun.

verses.text:
ततः प्रवृत्तः सुमहान्संग्रामः शोणितोदकः ।
तावकानां च समरे पाण्डवानां च भारत ॥

meaning.en: Then, O Bharata, a very great battle began, with blood for water, between your men and the Pandavas.
